sun.upright:
Aries Suns like being first, that clean feeling of starting something before anyone else has got their coat off. This card is cut from your own cloth. It's the decan of Mars in the first ten degrees of Aries, so its planet is your ruler standing in its own sign, strong and completely unforced, and when it lands on your Sun it's close to a mirror. Same fire, same forward lean. Fire on fire turns the volume up, and that's where the trouble starts.

Look at the man in the picture for a second. He's got a small globe in one hand and a staff in the other, a second staff fixed to the wall beside him, and he's standing still, working out how far to go. That weighing is the bit Aries skips. You get the wanting at full strength, and the choosing, deciding which of three good directions is actually yours, feels like being held back by the collar. I've seen a lot of Aries Suns with ten things started in a year, every one of them begun with first-day certainty. The card is asking which one you meant.

At work it tends to be the pitch you win and then lose interest in once the newness wears off. With money it's the bold plan funded on a first burst of enthusiasm and quietly dropped by the third month. With a friend it's the trip you swore you'd organise, because organising is slower than deciding and you'd already moved on. Pick the one aim you'd still want if nobody clapped, and give it a fortnight of steady, boring effort before you start anything else.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, an Aries Sun tends to spend all the fire on the launch and have nothing left for the long middle. Mars at home is strong either way, so the drive doesn't vanish. It scatters. You announce the big direction, enjoy the rush of having decided, and then the daily, unglamorous work of getting there bores you, so you start something new to get the rush back. Pride makes it hard to admit a plan was too big, and you'll defend it long after you've stopped working on it.

At work this shows as a run of ambitious beginnings on your record and not much you can point to as finished. Around money it's the gear or the course bought in the first flush and never used. Go back over what you've kicked off lately and find the one you'd still choose with the excitement gone. Carry that through a dull week on purpose, and see what it's like to finish something.

moon.upright:
Sitting with a feeling is the hard part for an Aries Moon. One arrives and you want to do something with it straight away, because holding it feels like a slow burn under the skin. This card belongs here in a very physical way. Its planet, Mars, rules Aries, and the card sits in the first ten degrees of the sign, so the restlessness it brings is familiar weather for you. The Two of Wands lands as a hunger to get further than where you are, and you'll feel it in your legs and your chest long before you've put it into words.

The friction is that this card wants a plan, and a plan means staying put long enough to weigh two options against each other. Fire feeding fire makes the itch louder, so what you get is the urge to leap and no patience for the map. You'll know the evening where you decide, all at once, that everything has to change, and by morning the certainty has cooled and you're a bit embarrassed about the messages you sent.

With a partner it can be the big declaration made hot and half-regretted by breakfast. In the body it's the workout started at full tilt and dropped when the novelty goes. Sleep suffers when there's an unmade decision rattling around, and you lie there planning escapes from a life that was fine yesterday. When the urge to overhaul everything hits, find the one small thing that set it off and deal with only that.
moon.reversed:
Restlessness you can't put a name to is how this card usually shows up reversed on an Aries Moon. The feeling still wants out at Mars speed, but whatever it was meant to push toward is blocked, so the heat comes out sideways as irritation with whoever's closest. Snapped answers over nothing. A short fuse you're ashamed of an hour later. Your body holds the unspent charge in a jaw that won't unclench and sleep that comes late.

At home it's the partner or housemate getting the sharp edge of a decision you haven't made yet. At work it's a Monday of furious energy and a flat, sulky Thursday. What helps is small and physical. Find one job you can start and finish with your hands, a shelf, a garden bed, a meal from scratch, and let your body feel something go from beginning to end. The mood usually lifts before you've worked out what it was about.

rising.upright:
Aries rising arrives already moving. People meet someone direct, quick to the point, a bit impatient with the small talk that comes before the real conversation. The card sits comfortably on that entrance, because Mars owns your rising sign and this card puts Mars at the very front of it, so the readiness it describes is the same readiness strangers already see in you. You've usually spotted the opening in a room before you've shaken anyone's hand.

Where it catches is that this card is about choosing where to go, and a fire Ascendant would sooner just go. Aries has The Emperor for its own Major, the one who decides by announcing it. The Two asks you to stand at the edge a moment and pick a direction on purpose. From the inside that pause can feel like dithering, and you'll be tempted to skip it. Fire on fire means you start at speed, and at speed it's easy to miss that you never really decided.

In a job interview it's the confidence that gets you in the door and the role that turns out not to be the one you wanted. On a first date you steer the whole evening while the other person goes quietly along with it. With a new landlord or a tradesperson it's the quick handshake deal that one more question would have improved. Before you launch into the next new thing with someone, ask them one real question and wait for the whole answer.
rising.reversed:
The fast start keeps misfiring when this card turns over on Aries rising. You come in strong and it reads as pushy, the offer taken as a demand, the plan pitched before anyone asked to hear it. Mars at the door wants the result before the introductions are done, and people who've been steamrolled before will put their guard up early. Sometimes it swings the other way and you hold the first move back completely, because a beginning that might land wrong feels worse to you than no beginning at all.

A new colleague gets the clipped version of you and writes you off as prickly before they've seen what you can do. A first date hears your list of requirements and feels interviewed. Open the next introduction with a genuine question, and let the other person talk for a good while before you say your piece.

sun.upright:
Taurus Suns build slowly and want what they build to last, solid enough to lean a whole life on. The Two of Wands turns up and starts an argument with that. Its planet is Mars, which is in detriment in Taurus, the sign opposite its home, so it has to work against the grain here, and the card's push to leave a secure position for a bigger one costs you effort other people seem to find for free. Aries and Taurus are next-door signs with almost nothing in common, neighbours who each have what the other lacks.

So the pull is real, and so is the resistance. You've made something good and stable, and this card is nudging you to risk part of it on something larger, and every instinct you've got says why would I. Fire and earth don't mix on their own. They have to be introduced, and that's what this card is doing, walking your steadiness up to an ambition it didn't ask for. It can feel like being hurried through a meal you wanted to take your time over, and you're entitled to find that annoying.

At work it's the safe role you're quietly outgrowing and the bolder one you keep talking yourself out of. With money you're the sensible saver who can't make the one investment in yourself, the course or the tools or the deposit. There's usually a project you've costed in your head for a year. Take the smallest version of the bigger move, the one that risks least, and put a date on it.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Taurus Sun digs in right where it ought to be loosening. Mars already works against the grain in this sign, and reversed it barely works at all, so the bigger plan becomes something you admire from a safe distance and never put real effort behind. You call it prudence. Often it's the fear that leaving a solid position means losing it for nothing, and fixed earth can sit on a good idea for years and call the sitting patience.

At work this is the reliable pair of hands who's stopped putting themselves forward and watches bolder colleagues take ground you could have had. With savings, it's keeping them so cautious they lose value while you wait for a certainty that doesn't come. Find the one move you keep deferring and take a first step you could undo if you had to. Do it before the wanting cools into something you used to think about.

moon.upright:
Comfort for a Taurus Moon is solid and physical, the same chair, a full fridge, a routine nobody moves. This card arrives like a knock at the door on a settled evening. Mars, its planet, is in detriment here, uneasy in an earth sign that wants nothing to change, so the restlessness the Two of Wands carries doesn't feel exciting to you. It's more of an itch you'd prefer not to have. Something in you is being asked to want more, and what you actually wanted was to be left in peace.

Fire and earth are strangers to each other. They don't blend on their own, so the urge to reach and your need for solid ground sit side by side and don't really speak. You'll feel it as a low unease on a perfectly good weekend, a sense that you should be doing something bigger, which gets chased off almost as soon as it arrives by how nice it is to do nothing. Taurus Moons are loyal to their comforts, and that's fine, though this card won't leave the question alone.

With a partner it can be a stretch where you're content and slightly walled in at once, and can't explain the second part. In the body it's comfort eating over a background hum of wanting change. At home there's the room you keep meaning to redo. When that unsettled feeling turns up, ask it what one small thing it wants moved. Move that, and leave the rest of your life where it is.
moon.reversed:
The card reversed on a Taurus Moon tends to soothe itself into a corner. The pull this card carries gets buried under the things that make you feel safe, the food, the familiar routine, the evening that looks exactly like last night's, and the wanting doesn't go away. It goes quiet and heavy. Mars, uneasy in an earth sign, turns its heat inward as stubbornness, a reluctance to be shifted even an inch off your spot.

In the body it's comfort that's tipped over into numbing, the extra helping, the third episode, the early night that doesn't actually rest you. Around money it's the small treats piling up on the statement while the real want goes unnamed. Before you reach for the usual soother, stop and ask what you need underneath it. The first answer is often a snack. Sit with it until a second answer turns up.

rising.upright:
People meeting a Taurus rising for the first time read calm, solid, someone who takes their time and is worth waiting for. You rarely rush a first impression. The Two of Wands drawn for your mask brings a planet that's uncomfortable here. Mars is in detriment in Taurus, so the card's appetite for a bold new start has to push against your natural setting, which is to be sure before you move. Strangers see someone weighing a big step with the handbrake gently on.

Taurus has The Hierophant for its own Major, the card of the proven way, and the Two is asking you to point at an untried horizon and go. That rub shows in how you start things with new people. You'll say you're thinking it over, and you genuinely are, and you keep thinking it over in the same careful loop while the opening quietly closes. Fire and earth need an introduction before they'll cooperate, and Taurus rising is slow to make introductions.

In a new job it's the bigger role that got mentioned in passing and never followed up, because a passing mention didn't feel solid enough to act on. In friendship it's the new person who suggested getting together twice and then went quiet. With a big purchase it's the good rate you compared against every other one until it expired. Answer the next real invitation within a day. Say yes to the first step only, and be as slow as you like about everything after it.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on Taurus rising, the calm that usually reassures people can harden into something that looks like refusal. You mean to seem steady and it comes across as dug in, an agreeable surface with nothing moving behind it, and a stranger walks away unsure whether you said yes, no, or nothing at all. Mars is uncomfortable in this sign, so even a small first commitment feels like a shove, and you smile, stall, and wait for the moment to pass.

At work this is the new manager who thinks you took something on when you were only being polite. With a big purchase it's the smooth salesperson who read your stalling as a yes, and the fine print you skimmed to get out of the room. When the next automatic yes is halfway out of your mouth, check whether you'd actually put a date against it. If you wouldn't, say you need a day, and then use the day.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns like to keep three conversations and two projects going and be quick at all of them. The Two of Wands feeds that easily. Aries, the card's sign, is sextile yours, a friendly two-sign gap that hands you an opening, and fire and air get on well, each one making the other catch faster, so ideas for bigger versions of your life arrive in bulk.

The catch is already in your own Major. The Lovers is really a card about choosing, and choosing is exactly what this card asks for. Mars visits Gemini without any rank and takes its colour from Mercury, so the card's drive tends to come out as talk and plans and clever framing, and a decided move is slower to show up. You can survey ten horizons brilliantly and commit to none, because picking one makes the other nine look better the instant you do. There's a nervier note as well. Mars rules the middle ten degrees of Gemini, the Nine of Swords decan, the three-in-the-morning card, so wanting more can flip into fretting over a choice until you're sick of it.

At work you're the one everyone wants in the ideas meeting and nobody quite trusts with delivery, which stings partly because it's a bit fair. In love you're wonderful company and hard to build a fixed plan around. Of all the bigger directions you've talked about lately, pick the one you'd still be proud of in a year, and give it your mornings for a month with the phone in another room.
sun.reversed:
A reversed Two can leave a Gemini Sun with plenty of cleverness and nowhere useful to put it. Mars borrowing Mercury's quickness turns into the very good reason the bigger plan hasn't started, an explanation shaped for whoever's asking, five half-projects that keep you from being judged on any one of them. You can talk yourself out of a door as smoothly as you talk other people through it, and that fluency is what hides the stall, from other people and from you.

In the job it's the update that sounds like progress and doesn't contain any. In a friendship it's the plan you retell in a slightly new shape each time, so the fact that it never happens always seems to be somebody else's doing. Notice the next time your own pitch runs smoother than you actually feel about it. Say the plain version out loud, even if the plain version is that nothing's moved, and don't tidy it up afterwards.

moon.upright:
Talking is how a Gemini Moon settles, turning a feeling into words and handing it to someone. This card lands as a pull toward something bigger, and because fire and air feed each other, that pull arrives already chattering, full of plans for a wider life said out loud before you've checked whether you actually want it. Mars has no dignity in Gemini, so its drive reaches you coloured by Mercury, and you feel it mostly as a busy, restless head.

The friction is that the Two of Wands needs you to stay with one direction long enough to feel it, and a Gemini Moon would sooner discuss every direction than settle into one. There's a darker foothold worth knowing about. Mars rules the middle decan of Gemini, the Nine of Swords, the card of lying awake, so when the wanting has nowhere to land it can turn into running the same decision round in loops at two in the morning. The sense that you ought to be going after something more, left unspent, becomes a mind that won't switch off.

With friends you might be the easy talker, the one who's always reachable and slow to admit anything's wrong, because you've already turned the restlessness into a good story. With sleep it's midnight planning of lives you may never live. When the words run out, leave the silence alone for a minute, see which of those bigger wants is still there, and say that one out loud.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Gemini Moon, this card leaves a mind with nobody at the wheel. The urge that wanted a direction dissolves into commentary, two inner voices bickering over every feeling, the phone picked up forty times, one more tab before sleep. Mars holds the Nine of Swords decan of your sign, the small-hours dread, so the unspent wanting sours into a worry that feels like thinking and settles nothing.

Friends get long voice notes at odd hours. A whole workday goes by where you touched everything and finished nothing, and your body pays with the skipped lunch and the clenched jaw. Give the spinning part something finite to do, a ten-minute walk with a fixed turnaround point, or the one phone call you keep dodging, so at least one thing gets to an end. The rest of the list can wait until morning.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising arrives talking, bright and quick and interested in everyone, and people warm to how easy you are to fall into conversation with. The Two of Wands sits well on that doorway. The card's sign is sextile yours, an easy opening between fire and air, so its forward lean and your quick tongue pull the same way. First meetings turn into plans, a passing remark turns into a project, and people can see you weighing something bigger and inviting them along.

The trouble is the one this card always brings, and your own Major, The Lovers, sharpens it, since both are about choosing. A mutable air Ascendant can start ten things in a fortnight and finish none of them. From your side each option still feels open, because you could always circle back and the person seemed keen enough. What you miss is how quickly other people's interest cools when nothing follows, and how the quiet verdict that you're all talk lands well before anyone says it.

At a work event it's the good contact left in a coat pocket. In dating it's the brilliant first evening that turns into a fortnight of witty messages and no second meeting, each of you waiting for the other to move. With a would-be collaborator it's the file you keep promising to send. Take the one plan you keep saying you'll get to and pin it to an actual day in the calendar.
rising.reversed:
People find a Gemini rising hard to pin down when this card is upside down. The easy fluency goes slippery, and you read as quick, charming and possibly not someone to rely on, fairly or not. Signals get crossed, and a fair few of them start with you. A light yes gets heard as a firm one. Sometimes there's a flicker of nerves under it too, and the usual quick talk deserts you at exactly the wrong moment.

On the job it's the colleague who's started quietly doubling whatever you estimate. In a new friendship it's the outing that was a definite yes and then evaporated, more than once. Take your first line slower than feels natural. Give one honest reason you're there and let it sit without decoration. If you feel a promise forming early in a conversation, hold onto it until you're nearly done talking.

sun.upright:
The Two of Wands is all appetite for leaving safe ground, and a Cancer Sun builds its life around the people it loves and wants to be the one keeping them safe. That's an awkward angle to start from. The card's planet, Mars, is in fall in Cancer, uncomfortable and not really heard, so the bold, self-directed push it carries arrives muffled and has to find an indirect way to do its work. Aries and Cancer are square, too, three signs apart, a friction that forces action even while it grinds.

Fire and water are opposites. Put them together and you get steam, or one puts the other out, and your ambition and your need to protect people really are at odds here. From the inside it feels like wanting something big for yourself and immediately hearing the objection, what about everyone who depends on me. So your ambition goes sideways, into other people's plans, and one day you look up and find you've helped everyone else get somewhere and stayed exactly where you were.

At work it's being the one who makes the team run and never the one who puts a hand up for the bigger role. With a partner it's knowing exactly how to grow their life and having no plan for your own. Most Cancer Suns I've read for have one thing they're quietly building with only their name on it, kept quiet because saying it out loud feels exposed. Tell one person you trust what yours is, before the old objection talks you out of it again.
sun.reversed:
Reversed for a Cancer Sun, the card tends to send your ambition underground, where it turns into resentment. Mars is already in fall in this sign, and upside down it stops even trying to come out straight, so instead of naming what you want you steer for it sideways, through hints, through doing so much for other people that they owe you, through a quiet martyrdom nobody asked for. The wanting is still there. It's just gone crab-wise and a bit sour.

At work it's the promotion you feel owed and won't put yourself forward for, and then mind when it goes to someone who did. With the person you love it's the evening you were hoping for and never mentioned, and the coldness when they failed to read your mind. Find one place where you've been angling for something by stealth, and ask for the actual thing, plainly, in one sentence.

moon.upright:
A Cancer Moon needs to feel held, and it needs to know everyone under the roof is all right. It feels things at high tide. This card brings a restless push to get out past the safe walls of home, and that push sits badly in you. Mars is in fall in Cancer, out of place and unheard, so the wanting doesn't come out as clean ambition. It comes out as moodiness, as a vague dissatisfaction you can't trace back to anything. Something wants more and can't say so directly.

Fire and water don't mix, one turns the other to steam, so this card's heat meeting your feelings can leave you churned up without knowing why. You'll feel the pull to strike out toward something bigger and, in the same breath, a wave of guilt or fear about leaving the nest, and the two cancel each other into a stuck, teary restlessness. The Chariot is Cancer's Major, the urge to go forward inside armour, and here you want to go forward and stay shut in your shell at the same time.

With a partner it's wanting a bigger life together and flinching at every actual step toward it. In your body the churn tends to land in the stomach, the appetite that goes off when something unspoken is moving. With family it's an old loyalty holding you right where you've outgrown. When the restlessness comes up, don't try to talk yourself out of it. Work out what small step wouldn't cost you your sense of safety, and take that one.
moon.reversed:
When the card's upside down, a Cancer Moon pulls the whole urge back inside the shell and lets it stew. With nowhere to go it becomes a churn, so you fall quiet and wait to be guessed, or you build a slow case against whoever seems to be standing in the way. Mars in fall can't move cleanly here, and the heat seeps out as moods, tides of hurt that turn up with no clear cause and take days to go back out.

With a partner it's the long freeze over something they haven't even noticed. At home it's dinner eaten in a silence with edges on it. The case in your head feels watertight because you've gone over it so many times, and that's the problem with it. Before you act on the story, test one piece of it out loud with the person it's about. Quite often they remember it differently.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising comes at the world sideways, feeling out the mood of a place before it'll commit, and strangers read you as gentle, watchful and a bit guarded. The Two of Wands drawn for your mask asks you to stand somewhere visible and pick a bold direction, which is a tall order for this Ascendant. Mars is in fall in Cancer, so the card's forward drive reaches your surface watered down, and what people see is caution with nerves underneath. You're looking at the far horizon with the front door held half shut.

Aries and Cancer are square, a friction that won't let you settle even while your instinct says retreat, so you feel shoved toward starting and tugged toward hiding at once. The card's fire and your water are opposite elements, and in you they mostly make steam. The Chariot is Cancer's own Major, forward motion behind armour, and a public start with no armour on feels almost improper to you. You'd much prefer to be brought in by a friend, or given a reason to be there, or to have met everyone once already.

At work it's the position you'd thrive in and never apply for cold, because an unsolicited approach feels like standing out in the open. Socially it's the circle that's asked you along twice and hasn't seen you yet, because there's no familiar face in it. In a new romance it's weeks of hoping they'll make the first move so you won't have to. Find one opening that needs you to introduce yourself and take it while the nerve's there. You're allowed to leave early.
rising.reversed:
The shell closes when this card reverses on Cancer rising, and it's slow to open again. The card wants you out in the open, starting something, and instead you pull back and read danger into new faces before they've given you any reason. Mars in fall makes your manner flip about, gentle one day and shut the next, so people can't predict which version of you is coming, and a good few give up guessing.

A newcomer at work takes your withdrawal for coldness when it's nerves. Someone you're drawn to reads the retreat after a warm evening as lack of interest and drifts off. Openings go by while you wait for a feeling of safety that usually arrives last. Choose one person and tell them in a plain sentence what you'd like from them, and send it while it's still a bit rough.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns want to be seen doing the thing they're proud of, and recognised for it without having to ask. The Two of Wands lands warmly here. Aries, the card's sign, is trine yours, four signs along in the same element, so the drive to go after something bigger reaches you with very little resistance, and fire on fire lifts the whole thing higher. Mars comes into Leo as a guest with no special rank, taking its colour from the Sun, so the card's ambition arrives dressed for an audience.

That's the gift and the snag together. Leo is fixed fire. Once you've chosen a direction you commit hard and shine at it, and fixed can also mean you only go for what you already know will be applauded. Mars rules the last ten degrees of your sign, the Seven of Wands decan, the card of holding your ground against all comers, so the urge to expand can turn into defending the position you've already got. You'll feel it as a boredom you can't explain, a life that looks impressive and hasn't actually grown in a while.

At work it's the role you could do in your sleep and the bolder one you won't chase, because being a beginner again feels beneath you. In love it's needing your partner impressed and going oddly flat when they're only pleased. With something creative it's the polished act, repeated. Pick one thing you'd be visibly bad at for a while, tell someone you're learning it, and let them watch.
sun.reversed:
A reversed Two can have a Leo Sun spending its energy on looking capable. Mars lit by the Sun gets very good at the appearance of ambition, the announced project with a beautiful logo and no second month, the confident answer to a question you didn't quite follow. Or pride flips it round and you won't attempt anything you might not shine at, which passes for high standards and is mostly a fear of being watched while you fumble.

At work it's a reputation slightly bigger than what you've actually delivered, and you can feel that gap even when nobody mentions it. Among friends it's taking over someone's story and telling it better than the person it happened to. Take on one job where the effort will be invisible to everyone. See it through, and don't mention it to anyone.

moon.upright:
A Leo Moon is fed by being noticed, by warm attention from someone who matters, by the feeling of having been chosen. The Two of Wands brings a pull toward a bigger life, and because Aries is trine your Moon sign, that pull comes easily, fire running into fire, so wanting more feels natural and even fun. Mars borrows the Sun's warmth in Leo, which makes the ambition generous and outward, the kind that wants to bring people along.

The tension is quieter than that. Fixed fire hangs on to whatever keeps it warm, a loyalty, a role, a way of being loved, so going after something new can be shadowed by a fear of losing the warmth you've already got. Mars holds the Seven of Wands decan of Leo, the instinct to guard your patch, so under the big generous plans there's often some watchfulness, a checking of who's still paying attention. You feel most yourself when you're expanding and most frightened at the exact moment you might have to leave a warm room to do it.

With a partner it's the grand shared dream that stalls the second it means less of their attention on you. With friends it's wanting to grow and needing the group to grow with you, and sulking a little if they won't. Tell the person whose attention you actually want what it is you're going after. Leo Moons usually get braver once they've been heard.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on a Leo Moon, the card can turn feelings into a performance, and then you resent the audience it drew. Mars under the Sun makes a good story out of every hurt, told well and told often, and the retelling slowly stands in for what actually happened. Or pride slams it all shut, and you go bright and busy and fine, and nobody's let near the sore spot, including the people who could help.

Friends notice the same wound has been aired three times to three people, improved a little each round. A partner notices you're sunny with everyone except them. Sleep goes shallow. If one person genuinely hurt you, tell them the plain version once. After that, stop passing it around, and see how quickly it loses its charge.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks in as though it was expected, and usually it was. People meet warmth, a bit of show, someone who'll lift the mood of the room. This card is a comfortable fit on that entrance. Aries trines your rising sign and fire feeds fire, so you come across as someone visibly ready to go after something bigger, and it looks good on you. Mars, a guest of the Sun here, gives the ambition a bright, slightly performed edge.

Where it rubs is that Leo rising is fixed. It settles on an act that works and runs it, and the Two wants you pointing at new ground and moving. Mars holds the Seven of Wands decan in your sign, the stance of defending what you've got, so a strong first impression can quietly turn into guarding your image. Strangers meet the confident version and take a while to find out whether there's a real plan behind it or only the pose of one.

At an interview it's the presence that wins the room, and then a follow-up that has to prove it wasn't all delivery. A first date can be two hours of wonderful company without either of you saying anything true. In a new group it's being liked fast and taken seriously slowly. Next time you meet someone who matters, drop the entrance you know works and let them see you actually deciding something, even if it comes out a bit rough.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on Leo rising, the entrance runs ahead of the person making it. Big arrival, big promises, the easy confidence that gets you through the door, and then people wait for the follow-through the entrance implied. Mars borrowing the Sun's shine makes it easy to promise and harder to deliver. Or the confidence deserts you and you run the act on autopilot, smile on and nobody home, hoping nobody notices the difference.

At work it's the pitch that won the client and the colleague now stuck delivering it, who's started to mind. Socially it's being the one who made the night and going home feeling oddly invisible. Undersell yourself a little at your next few first meetings. Say less about what you're going to do, and let people find out the rest by watching.

sun.upright:
Being useful matters to a Virgo Sun, and so does getting things right, being the one who can actually fix it. The Two of Wands asks for something that doesn't come naturally, which is to go after a big, half-mapped future before the details are pinned down. Aries and Virgo are quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common, the kind of angle that never quite settles and needs constant small adjustment. So the card's wide horizon and your need to check the footing keep having to be renegotiated.

Mars visits Virgo without any dignity, coloured by Mercury, so the ambition comes through as analysis, as planning, as a spreadsheet for the leap you haven't taken. Fire and earth are neutral, no natural warmth and no clash, and they simply have to be introduced. Virgo's own Major is The Hermit, who goes off alone to perfect the work, and the pull between refining in private and moving in public is most of your tension with this card. You can prepare a bold move so thoroughly that the preparing becomes the whole activity.

Professionally it's the plan that's better than anyone's and a fortnight late because it wasn't perfect yet. With money it's the careful budget where the one real investment in yourself keeps missing the cut. With your health it's the routine designed down to the minute and never quite begun. Let the bigger plan leave your desk while it's still a bit rough, and send it to one person who can do something with it.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun with this card reversed points all its skill at the flaws, and the launch keeps slipping. Mars through Mercury turns into the critic who makes nothing, the edit on someone else's work, the private list of everything wrong with your own plan kept running late into the evening. It feels like being responsible. Mostly it's a way of never having to put the bigger plan out there and be judged on it.

At work it's fixing a colleague's document while your own ambitious project hasn't moved in a month. At home it's the partner who stopped asking for help because the help came back with notes. Spend one full day correcting nobody, including yourself, and put that spare attention into one piece of the plan you keep putting off.

moon.upright:
A tidy drawer, a checked plan, a small job finished. That's what makes a Virgo Moon feel safe. This card wants something close to the opposite, a move toward something bigger with the details still loose, and that unsettles you somewhere below thought. Mars has no standing in Virgo and comes coloured by Mercury, so the wanting arrives as mental restlessness, a mind that keeps turning the possible move over, looking for the flaw before it'll let you feel excited.

Aries and Virgo sit at a quincunx, always a little out of step, so the ambition and your need to have everything accounted for never quite line up, and you adjust and adjust. Fire and earth are neutral, with no easy warmth between them, and mostly the card gives your worry a bigger subject. You'll recognise the version where an exciting plan turns, within the hour, into a list of everything that could go wrong with it.

With a partner it's showing love by sorting out the thing they were dreading, and never quite saying you want more for the two of you. In the body it lands as a tight stomach and sleep broken at three by a running list. With work it's the safe, excellent job and a quiet ache to stretch that you keep filing under later. When the list starts, write down the one part of the plan you could actually test, and do only that part.
moon.reversed:
Carefulness turns into anxiety for a Virgo Moon when this card is reversed, and from the outside it looks like diligence. Mars through Mercury, pointed inward, audits every feeling the card stirs up. Was that a reasonable thing to want, is this restlessness a warning, should you have started already. There's a lot of thinking and very little comfort, and the routines that usually settle you start to feel like rules you keep failing.

Sleep shows it first, then digestion, then your patience with the people who love you. A partner might hear the fifth question about the same small worry and not know what to say. Your body gets the rigid version of good habits, the skipped treat, the extra check. Let one routine slip for a week on purpose, the bed unmade, lunch unplanned, and see that the day holds together anyway.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising comes across composed and a touch reserved, the one who noticed the typo, your shoes, and where the exit is. This card asks you to stand up somewhere visible and commit to a big plan, which sits awkwardly with an Ascendant that likes to be fully ready before it's seen. Aries and Virgo are quincunx, an angle with nothing in common that calls for constant small adjustment, so the card's boldness and your carefulness never quite fit and you spend energy fine-tuning the join.

Mars comes in through Mercury here, so what people meet is ambition expressed as precision, the plan laid out neatly before any passion shows. Fire and earth are only neutral, so there's no natural spark, just two forces slowly learning to cooperate. Virgo has The Hermit, who perfects things in private, and the Two wants something public and unfinished, which feels almost rude to you. You'd much prefer to show people the polished result.

In a new job it's the competence that gets you handed the admin and passed over for the bold brief. In friendship it's being the reliable one and rarely the one people ring for a laugh, though you're funny. With a big decision, a move or a career change, it's the pros-and-cons list that keeps growing while the window shrinks. In the next room that matters, lead with the bigger idea and hold the caveats back until someone asks for them.
rising.reversed:
The first few minutes come out stiff for Virgo rising with this card upside down. The precision that normally makes people trust you reads as chilly or fussy, because Mars through Mercury is busy heading off mistakes when it could be meeting whoever you're talking to. You might hear yourself correcting something a stranger said before you even know their surname. Or the care tips into near-silence, and they end up inventing a version of you to fill the quiet.

A new manager can take your careful questions for doubt. Someone on a first date can take the exactness for being judged. Whether that's fair or not, it's what's coming across. Ease off one thing on purpose. Leave a typo where it lands, or let a half-told story stay half-told, and watch what the other person does with the gap.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns want things fair and pleasant, and they want to be liked while making them so, which is harder than it sounds. The Two of Wands puts a very Aries demand in front of you, because Aries is the sign directly opposite yours, the far end of the me-and-you axis. This card is about deciding what you want and going after it. The opposition pulls you toward balance, toward weighing what you want against everyone it might touch, and Mars is in detriment in Libra, working against the grain, so plain self-interest costs you an effort other people spend without noticing.

Fire and air are friendly, so ideas move fast and you can see every angle of the choice at once, which is exactly why you stall. Your own Major is Justice, scales in one hand and a sword in the other. Everyone remembers the scales and forgets the sword, the part where the decision actually comes down. You'll know the feeling of standing in front of three good doors and wanting to keep them all ajar so nobody, you included, has to miss out.

At work it's being the diplomat in every dispute and never quite pushing your own proposal through. In love it's understanding your partner's side so well that yours never gets said. With friends it's the holiday you arranged for everyone and didn't enjoy, because nobody asked where you wanted to go. Take the choice you keep gracefully putting off, give it a deadline, and tell the people it affects plainly and warmly, with a shorter explanation than you'd normally give.
sun.reversed:
Charm becomes a way of dodging for a Libra Sun with this card reversed. Mars in detriment gives up wanting anything for itself, and Venus's grace fills the gap, so you agree to keep the peace, swallow the opinion, take on the favour you'll resent, and the bigger direction that was actually yours never gets named. It adds up quietly over months, until people like you a great deal and can't say what you stand for.

At work it's being agreeable in the meeting and privately furious at the outcome. In a relationship it's resentment that seems to come from nowhere and has in fact been saved up since the start of the year. Pick one thing you've been softening to keep things smooth, and say all of it, kindly, to the person who needs to hear it.

moon.upright:
Discord in the house gets straight into a Libra Moon's body. What you need is peace, and in particular you need the people you love to be getting on. The Two of Wands brings a push toward something of your own, and that push comes from Aries, the sign opposite your Moon, which stands for exactly the self-interest a Libra Moon finds hard to feel entitled to. Mars is in detriment here, so wanting things for yourself stays quiet and is easy to talk down. Fire and air are friendly, so you can put what you want into words beautifully, and you can reason yourself right out of it just as well.

That's the trap. The opposition is a pull toward balance, and you tend to answer it by making sure everyone else is looked after first, so your own plans wait at the back of the queue. Venus rules your Moon sign and wants things to feel harmonious, and a big self-directed want doesn't feel harmonious at all. It feels selfish, so it gets shelved before it's been looked at properly.

With a partner it's always being the first to patch things up and never asking for the same back. Among friends it's quietly holding the group together, reading every message for the tone behind it. In your body it's the flat exhaustion after even a lovely gathering, the cost of all that balancing nobody saw you do. When the pull toward something of your own turns up, give it a full day before you start measuring it against what everyone else needs.
moon.reversed:
Every feeling goes through a committee first when this card reverses on a Libra Moon. Mars in detriment won't simply want a thing, so each emotion gets weighed for fairness and phrasing until it stops being a feeling and turns into an argument. On a bad stretch you can genuinely lose track of what you feel, because nothing seems valid until someone else has nodded it through.

With a partner it shows as endless checking of what they'd prefer, and a low simmer when they answer. With friends it's the reply drafted and redrafted into blandness and then never sent. Your body keeps count with a stiff neck after an evening that went perfectly well. When someone next asks how you are, answer briefly and honestly, and leave off the joke you'd usually use to take the edge off.

rising.upright:
Libra rising arrives graceful and easy to talk to, the one who makes the introductions and remembers everyone's name. This card plays into the charm and then asks the hard thing, because Aries opposes your rising sign, and Aries is all about knowing what you want and going straight for it. A Libra Ascendant tends to start by matching the other person, their tone, their pace, sometimes their opinions, and the card wants you to bring your own aim in first. Mars in detriment makes that effortful, though fire and air being friendly means that once you do speak up, it lands well.

It costs you in a specific way. You mirror so smoothly that people leave a first meeting having met a very agreeable version of what they already think, and they've learned almost nothing about what you're after. The opposition keeps tugging you toward the middle, and a beginning usually needs you a bit off-centre and clear. Justice is your own Major, and people forget that the figure on that card is there to make a ruling.

In a negotiation it's the deal that felt lovely and left you short. On a first date it's being so tuned to them that they go home knowing nothing real about you. In a new role it's being well liked from day one and consulted on nothing that matters. Before you next sit down with someone new, decide one thing you want from the meeting, and make sure it gets said in the first ten minutes.
rising.reversed:
With this card reversed, Libra rising's smooth surface can look as though there's nothing underneath it. Mars in detriment lets the charm run while the substance drops away, so a stranger leaves the first meeting fond of you and unable to name one thing you believe. The temptation is to give everyone the version of you they'll like best, and it wears you out, and it comes apart the day two of those people end up in the same room.

At work, sooner or later, someone finds out you agreed with two people who wanted opposite things. Socially it's the string of yeses you gave out of politeness and are now quietly wriggling out of. When you next meet someone new, put one real opinion on the table early, one they might push back on, and let them push.

sun.upright:
This card is interesting on a Scorpio Sun. Its planet, Mars, also rules Scorpio, so the card turns up with the authority of your own landlord, only this time Mars is coming at you from its fire sign, and you're its water one. You want to get to the bottom of things and be the one who can't be fooled, and you do it with a depth other people find slightly unnerving. The bold survey of new ground that the Two of Wands describes is real in you. It just runs underground, strategic and private, sized up long before anyone sees you move.

The friction is elemental. The card is fire and your sign is water, opposites that make steam or put each other out, so the open, declared ambition the Two wants sits oddly against your instinct to reveal nothing until you're sure. Aries and Scorpio share a ruler and almost nothing else, a quincunx that keeps needing small adjustments. Mars also holds the Five of Cups decan at the start of your sign, the card of loss, so whenever you go after something there's a wariness about what committing might cost.

At work it's having a plan nobody has heard, held close until the moment it wins. In love it's knowing your partner's moods better than they do and guarding your own. Money tends to get the same treatment, a quiet strategy running under a calm surface. Take one thing you've quietly worked out and put all of it in front of the person it would most help, keeping nothing back for later.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun can go cold and tactical when this card turns over. Mars stays strong in your sign even upside down, so the drive doesn't weaken. It goes quiet, and instead of moving toward the bigger thing in the open you bank what you know, set tests nobody signed up for, and use silence to make other people overcommit. It tends to work, and it leaves you lonelier than you'd ever say.

At work it's sitting on something useful until it can be spent for advantage, and the trust that leaves the room once people catch on. In love it's a ledger of every slight, kept with dates. Work out what you're holding back and what the holding is costing you. Then give one piece of it away, openly, to someone who'd be glad of it.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon feels everything all the way down and hands the key to very few people. What you need is loyalty, privacy and the truth, roughly in that order. This card brings a pull to go past your safe depths toward something bigger, and because Mars rules Scorpio, that pull comes with real force. It's your own planet asking. The trouble is that it's a fire card landing in deep water, and the two don't blend, so the wanting churns everything up.

Aries and Scorpio are quincunx, close only in sharing Mars, forever adjusting to each other, so the bold outward move and your need to keep your inner world sealed keep pulling in different directions. Mars also holds the Five of Cups decan at the start of your sign, the card of old grief, so the fear under the wanting is often about loss, about what a bigger, more exposed life might take from you. You want more and brace for the price in the same breath.

With a partner it shows as a longing to go deeper that comes out as testing them. With family it's the buried thing a braver life would mean finally naming. At night it can show as vivid dreams doing the reaching your waking self won't. Tell the person you trust most one true thing you've never said out loud. Keep it short, and leave the rest for a day you choose.
moon.reversed:
Upended, a Scorpio Moon takes the whole urge underground and lets it brood. Mars in your sign, turned inward, plots and rehearses and reads hidden meanings into every message, and you become certain you know what's going on in someone else's head. You might be partly right, and you're not checking. The Five of Cups decan pulls it toward old grief, so a present fear gets fused with a much older one.

It surfaces as a suspicion no reassurance can touch, or a quiet in the house that everyone feels and nobody will name. Sleep goes restless and the three o'clock certainties get very convincing. Someone you love may be treading carefully around you without knowing why. Ask the person, straight out, about the thing you've been decoding, and then take their answer as true for a week before you let yourself reinterpret it.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising comes across watchful and hard to read, and people often feel seen by you before they've said much. The Two of Wands on that doorway carries your own ruler, since Mars rules Scorpio, so there's real authority in how you weigh a new beginning, a quiet, sharp confidence at the start of things. You say little, what you say lands, and you've usually read the room before it's read you.

What pulls against it is that this card is about the open hand, the whole plan laid out where everyone can see it, and a Scorpio Ascendant would sooner keep the table covered. It's fire against water, so the card's readiness to declare and your instinct to conceal rub against each other. The angle to Aries is a quincunx, an awkward five-sign gap, so the bold public start the card wants never sits easily on your guarded entrance. Small talk, in particular, you find close to pointless, and people can tell.

At an interview it's the short, exact answer that slightly unnerves the panel. In dating it's the intensity people find magnetic on the first night and hard work by the third if nothing's opened up. Starting somewhere new, you can earn a reputation for being formidable in the first week by saying almost nothing. When you next meet someone, hand over one small, ordinary fact about yourself early on, what you did at the weekend or what you're reading, and give it plainly.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising already keeps people at arm's length, and with this card upside down the watchfulness tips into distrust. Mars scans each new person for the catch, and they can feel the appraisal the moment they walk in. Or you give off an intensity you never meant to, and a quiet you intended as neutral gets taken as a verdict against them. People who are shy themselves tend to take it hardest.

At work it's newcomers keeping a careful distance, which you then take as evidence they've got something to hide. In friendship it's putting people through quiet tests and losing the good ones, who won't sit for them. With a new neighbour it's the greeting you didn't return. Next time you meet a stranger, say one honest reaction to the conversation while it's happening, out loud, a beat before it feels safe to.

sun.upright:
Reaching for a wider life is about the most Sagittarian thing there is, so this card lands very naturally on a Sagittarius Sun. Aries is trine your sign, four signs along in the same fire, so the Two of Wands and your own drive point the same way, and fire on fire makes the whole thing bigger. Mars comes into Sagittarius as a guest, coloured by Jupiter, and the ambition arrives already inflated, generous, sure there's more out there. You're here to find the bigger meaning and keep moving toward it.

That's exactly the risk. The Two of Wands is about choosing one direction and committing, and Jupiter loves to keep the whole horizon open, so you can survey the world with real appetite and never decide which way to walk. Your own Major is Temperance, the patient mixing of things, and it's the quality you most need and least enjoy, because it asks you to stay with one plan long enough for it to become real. Sagittarius Suns I've known are usually planning the next country before they've unpacked in this one.

In your work it's the vision everyone loves and the follow-through nobody can find. In study it's three courses started and the dull middle module of each abandoned. In love it's the big shared future described beautifully and never begun. Take the plan you talk about most, work out a first step small enough to finish in an afternoon, and do it before you describe the vision to one more person.
sun.reversed:
The wrong way up, a Sagittarius Sun can mistake the pitch for the progress. Mars through Jupiter inflates everything, so the plan becomes a headline with no article under it, a bold forecast you half believe as it leaves your mouth, and your own conviction is what sells it to everyone else. Usually the size of the claim has grown while the work behind it hasn't moved.

On the job it's the grand announcement that now gets a polite nod and no questions, because people have learned to wait and see. With friends it's the adventure that's been three years in the talking. Choose one thing you've promised, and either take its first real step or say plainly that it isn't happening. Either answer lets the people waiting on you get on with their own plans.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room, the sense that life is bigger than this week and there's always somewhere else to go. The Two of Wands feeds that directly. Aries trines your Moon sign, so the pull toward more arrives as pure appetite, fire lifting fire, a restlessness that feels a lot like hope. Mars comes in flavoured by Jupiter, which makes the wanting expansive and warm, forever certain the good thing is just over the next hill.

The catch is that a big feeling and a chosen direction are different things, and this Moon tends to feel the wanting and skip the choosing. Fire feeding fire makes the itch to move louder, and Jupiter tells you it'll all work out, so an uncomfortable feeling can get answered by booking a trip or quitting something, and the thing that was actually wrong never gets looked at. Temperance is your sign's Major, the slow mixing you find genuinely dull, and it holds what you keep dodging, which is staying put long enough to know what you feel.

With a partner it's being cheerful about a problem that's really bothering you, and wanting space the second the conversation gets specific. Among friends it's being the one always up for an adventure and hard to reach when things go flat or sad. In the body it's the need to move, to walk it off. So go and walk it off, and somewhere on the way home put your finger on the one specific thing that set the restlessness going.
moon.reversed:
Every feeling becomes a lesson before it's been felt when the card reverses on a Sagittarius Moon. Mars through Jupiter reaches inward and hands you the philosophy, everything happens for a reason, it'll all come good, while the plain hurt sits under all that wisdom untouched. When the sermon won't hold, restlessness takes over, and you stay in motion so there's never a quiet enough moment to notice what's wrong.

At home it looks like plans torn up at the last minute and a partner worn out by never knowing what's happening. Among friends it's the bad month retold as comedy, so polished nobody thinks to check how you are underneath it. Before the next big change or escape, give yourself ten still minutes and name exactly what you're running from. Do it in front of someone if you possibly can.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes in open and friendly, a bit loud, up for whatever's going, and people warm to that straight away. This card fits it naturally. Aries trines your rising sign, the two fire signs are on easy terms, and people can see at once that you're up for something bigger. The enthusiasm is catching. Mars arrives coloured by Jupiter, which puts your appetite for the next big thing right there on the surface for everyone to see.

The trouble is that a mutable fire Ascendant opens with the grand gesture, the sweeping plan, the promise made in the warmth of the moment, and the Two wants you to actually choose one and stand by it. Jupiter oversells, so you can wave at a huge horizon at a first meeting and quietly dread the follow-up later. Temperance, your Major, is the patience to see one thing through, and to be honest that's what strangers end up judging you on, whether the big talk turned into anything.

In a new job it's the spark everyone loves at the start and the trail of unanswered messages a month later. Travelling, it's the impulsive booking with a clause you never read. In a new friendship it's the wonderful plan offered on the spot while the other person waits to see if you meant it. Before the next big yes leaves your mouth, put one practical question to it, even if asking lets a bit of air out of the moment.
rising.reversed:
The warm first impression can start working against Sagittarius rising. The broad, easy talk that usually throws doors open lands as bluster, or as the blunt remark dropped in front of exactly the wrong person, Mars through Jupiter overshooting the mark. Or the promises come out so generous that the plain reality afterwards can only disappoint, and people who liked you on the night feel a little conned by the following week.

Professionally it's the client holding you to a pledge you've half forgotten making. Socially it's the joke that misfired with someone you'd barely met, and the apology that never came. Take the first few minutes much slower than feels natural. Ask something, let the answer finish, and commit to nothing until you've met a second time.

sun.upright:
Mars is exalted in Capricorn, which makes this one of the better cards a Capricorn Sun can draw. Exaltation means the planet is an honoured guest, at its most idealised, and here the card's drive is ambition with the recklessness filed off, a plan already attached. You want to build something that lasts and be respected for having built it, and you'll wait years for the payoff. When you decide to expand, you tend to actually do it.

The friction is that Aries squares Capricorn, a hard angle that forces action, so the card's raw impatience grinds against your instinct to control the timing. You want the bold move and you want it perfectly sequenced, and those two don't always fit. Mars rules the middle decan of your sign, the Three of Pentacles, the card of skilled work done properly, so your ambition is happiest as a craft, built step by careful step. Your own Major is The Devil, and the shadow it warns about is letting the climb take over the whole of you.

At work it's the sound long-term plan and the bolder side idea you dismissed as not serious enough. With money it's being very sensible and a little afraid to spend on anything that won't pay back. With a parent or a mentor it's still quietly working to earn approval you may already have. Take up one thing that earns nothing and proves nothing, something you can be cheerfully bad at, and give it an hour a week.
sun.reversed:
Turned over, the card can make a Capricorn Sun's ambition into cold arithmetic. Mars is exalted in your sign and stays strong upside down, but the strength goes chilly, sizing people up for what they're worth to you, running a friendly chat like a negotiation. Or it flips the other way and the plan stalls, because you've decided you're too junior or not qualified enough to begin.

At work it's waiting for a permission nobody actually has to give you, or claiming the win a shade too smoothly. At home it's one more night on the laptop because that's easier than a real conversation. In friendship it's the catch-up postponed until life quietens down, and it doesn't. Take the one move you've been saving for when you're ready, and make it a month early.

moon.upright:
Being in control is what makes a Capricorn Moon feel safe, that and having proved it can cope without help. The Two of Wands brings an appetite to stretch toward something larger, and because Mars is exalted in Capricorn, that pull comes to you as competence, a want that already knows how it would go about getting there. You're likelier to cost it out quietly than to daydream about it. Feeling and plan arrive together, which is a real strength.

The strain comes from the square to Aries, a friction that won't let you sit still and yet grinds against your need to manage the pace. Fire and earth are only neutral, so the wanting doesn't warm you. It sets you a task. Mars holds the Three of Pentacles decan of your sign, which makes any ambition feel most bearable as work, something to build, and that's also how a Capricorn Moon hides. Turn a feeling into a project and you never have to just feel it. The Devil is your Major, and it knows how easily coping turns into a cage.

In a relationship it's handling the hard practical thing beautifully and never mentioning you were frightened. In the body it's pushing through tiredness because stopping feels like weakness. With family it's the old role of the responsible one, still running the show. When a want turns into another job on your list, stop and let yourself want it plainly for a day before you start managing it.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Capricorn Moon grinds the whole thing into duty. Mars exalted keeps working long after the warmth has gone, so the pull toward something bigger becomes one more standard to fail against, and you drive yourself at it with no pleasure in the going. The lighter parts of wanting, the play, the hope, get squeezed out, and what's left is obligation.

Physically it's pushing on through clear signs to stop, and treating rest as a reward you have to earn. At home it's being there in body and miles away, your mind still at the desk. With your partner it's turning every shared plan into a project to be managed. Do one small thing for no reason except that you'd enjoy it, and don't make it useful.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising meets the world with a straight face and a bit of reserve, and people read you as capable and serious, someone who's probably already thought it through. The card is well placed here. Mars is exalted in Capricorn, so the ambition you show is measured and believable, the kind that looks like it'll deliver. Strangers hand you responsibility quickly, because you look like someone who can be trusted with the bigger job.

What pulls against it is Aries squaring your rising sign, a friction that pushes you to start before you feel ready and clashes with your habit of waiting until you've earned the right. Fire and earth stay neutral, so there's no easy spark, just the slow work of getting a bold start moving. Mars in your Three of Pentacles decan means you start best by building where people can see the craft. Your own Major, The Devil, shows how easily you put things off while waiting for a permission nobody's actually withholding.

In a new role it's waiting to be handed authority you could simply take. Socially it's being respected before you're warmed to, and minding the gap more than you let on. With a big move it's a readiness that never quite feels ready. Do one thing you'd do if the title you're working toward were already yours, and do it before anyone says you can.
rising.reversed:
Strangers can take Capricorn rising for cold when this card is upside down. The seriousness that usually earns respect starts to feel like distance, and Mars, exalted but turned over, makes you so controlled on first meeting that people can't find a way in. You give little away, so they decide you're unapproachable before they've had a chance to be wrong about it.

At a new workplace it's being taken for stern when you're only reserved, and the team saving its jokes for someone else. On a first date the same caution reads as lack of interest. With a new group it's standing slightly apart and calling it professionalism. Let one unguarded thing show early, a small enthusiasm or an ordinary worry, the kind of thing you'd tell a friend.

sun.upright:
An Aquarius Sun wants to be its own person and to matter to something bigger than itself, ideally both at once. The Two of Wands suits that. Aries is sextile your sign, a friendly opening two signs along, and fire and air feed each other, so a wider future comes to you as ideas, as vision, a picture of how things could be. Mars visits Aquarius coloured by Saturn, or by Uranus if you use the modern ruler, so the ambition is either principled and patient or suddenly electric, depending on the day.

The snag is a fixed sign's snag. You can commit hard to the idea of a plan and be strangely slow to move your own body toward it, because Aquarius is happiest a step back, thinking, and the Two of Wands wants a hand on the actual world. Your Major is The Star, all hope and far horizon. It's a lovely card, and it can also keep you gazing at the future while the first ordinary step into it goes untaken.

At work it's the brilliant proposal for how the whole system should change and a reluctance to do the unglamorous first bit yourself. With friends it's having plans for everyone and being vague about your own. With a cause you care about, the principle tends to run ahead of the practice. Pick the piece of your big idea that only you can start, and start it with your own hands.
sun.reversed:
Aquarius Suns with this card reversed tend to keep the vision and hand off the doing. Mars through Saturn goes cool and stubborn, so the plan turns into a theory you defend, and being right about how it should work quietly replaces building it. Or the Uranian side flares and you tip over a good plan just to prove you won't be predictable.

At work it's the sharp critique of everyone else's approach and no finished thing of your own on the table. With friends it's being the one who sees clearly and stays oddly uninvolved. With a cause it's principle that never quite becomes a Tuesday afternoon of dull effort. Take the least visionary, most practical part of your big idea and do it yourself, before you improve anyone else's version.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs room to breathe and a bit of distance, even from people it loves, and it's calmest when feelings can be thought about. The Two of Wands stirs an urge to go after something larger, and since Aries is sextile your Moon sign, with fire and air on good terms, the pull arrives as a cool, clear idea of a wider life. You tend to know what you're reaching for before you feel much about it.

The difficulty is that wanting something usually asks for some heat, some willingness to want messily, and a fixed air Moon keeps its feelings at arm's length. Mars comes coloured by Saturn or Uranus, so the wanting is either dutiful and delayed or abrupt and out of nowhere, a sudden need for change that surprises even you. The Star, your Major, holds the calm hope this Moon runs on, and it can also let you watch your own life from a distance.

In a relationship it's offering clear-eyed advice when what's wanted is closeness. With friends it's being the trusted one everyone opens up to and rarely the one who does. In the body it's noticing you're run down as though you were reading it off a chart. When you feel the pull, let yourself want the thing warmly and a bit unreasonably before you talk yourself into the sensible version.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, the card has an Aquarius Moon handling the whole thing by floating above it. Mars through Saturn cools the wanting into analysis, so you diagnose the restlessness, file it under interesting, and decline to be moved by it. The Uranian streak can flip that into a sudden, cold decision to cut something off, made from a chilly distance, and it surprises the people it lands on.

With your partner it's going unreachable exactly when closeness is needed, there in body and gone in every other way. With friends it's the wise detachment that starts to feel like absence. Physically it's ignoring what your body is telling you because feelings are inconvenient. Say one thing you actually feel about it, plainly and warmly, to one person, before you retreat back into the theory.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising meets people in a friendly, slightly detached way, curious about everyone and close to nobody too fast, and you often come across as a bit different, which you tend to like. The card sits well on that. Aries is sextile your rising sign and fire feeds air, so you present as someone with an eye on a bigger, unconventional future, full of where things could go. Mars arrives through Saturn, or Uranus on the modern reading, so your ambition looks either coolly principled or unpredictable.

The rub is that a fixed air Ascendant leads with the idea and can forget there's a body attached that has to walk through the door. The Two wants a real first step, and you can hover in the concept of it, discussing the plan with anyone and committing to none of the ordinary moves it needs. The Star is your Major, and its far, hopeful horizon is exactly where your gaze goes, sometimes so far ahead that the person you're talking to feels a little unmet.

At a work event it's the fascinating conversation about the future that leads to no actual plan. In dating it's connecting on ideas and staying oddly hard to reach in person. In a new group it's being liked for your mind and kept at a slight distance. When you next meet someone who matters, come down from the big picture and tell them one plain thing you want next.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising's friendly distance can tip into cold when this card turns over. The individuality that usually intrigues people reads as aloofness or as being contrary on purpose, and Mars through Saturn makes you so detached at first that others can't tell whether you want them there. Or the Uranian edge shows and you come across as unpredictable, hard to build anything steady on.

At a new workplace it's being seen as the clever outsider and left out of the ordinary warmth. A first date goes brilliantly on ideas and leaves them unsure you even liked them. Among new people it's mistaking distance for independence. Let one ordinary, human thing show early, a small liking, some plain interest in the person, so people have somewhere warm to start.

sun.upright:
A Pisces Sun lives with the boundaries turned down, feeling its way through the world by imagination and sympathy, dreaming things before deciding them. The Two of Wands asks for something that doesn't come easily, which is fixing on one clear direction and driving at it. Aries sits right next door to Pisces, and neighbouring signs share almost nothing, so the card's sharp will and your soft, tidal nature are close on the calendar and strangers in temperament. Mars comes coloured by Jupiter, or Neptune on the modern reading, and the ambition gets dreamier, larger, harder to pin to a single plan.

Fire and water are opposites, steam or one dousing the other, so a plan can either evaporate into fantasy or feel like it's putting out your gentler fire. There's a warm foothold, though. Mars holds the Ten of Cups decan at the end of your sign, the card of a contented, connected life, so what you most truly want is often belonging and shared happiness, and winning something comes a long way second. Your own Major is The Moon, all dream and tide, and it can leave the vision gorgeous and the first step nowhere in sight.

In the job it's the beautiful idea that never gets a deadline. With money it's the vagueness that hopes it'll sort itself out. With a creative gift it's the thing you imagine in full and never quite begin. Take one dream you keep floating and give it a single unromantic, concrete edge, a date, a name, a first line.
sun.reversed:
In reverse, a Pisces Sun can let the whole plan drift off into fantasy. Mars through Neptune loosens the wanting until it's all daydream and no direction, and you can spend hours in the fully imagined version of the bigger life without taking the small real step toward it. It can slide further, into a fog where nothing's quite your fault and nothing quite gets started, and the drift feels almost like peace.

At work there's a vision board with no first task under it. With money it's the figures you'd rather not look at directly. In love it's idealising a future that stays safely imaginary. Pick the one part of the dream that an ordinary action could make real, and take that action, clumsily, before you've had time to think it over.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon feels everything, its own and everyone else's, with very little wall in between, and it needs regular retreat to stay well. The Two of Wands sets off a pull toward something larger, and it lands oddly in you, because Aries is the sign next door, a semi-sextile with little in common, so its clean, self-directed drive feels almost foreign to your gentle, merging way of feeling. Mars comes flavoured by Jupiter or Neptune, so the wanting is diffuse and romantic, easier to feel than to aim.

The card is fire and your Moon is water, and they don't blend. A want can dissolve the moment you try to hold it firmly, or the card's push can feel like a harshness you flinch from. Mars sits in your Ten of Cups decan, the dream of a warm, shared life, so what you're really after is usually connection and feeling safe, and only rarely some hard achievement. The Moon is your own Major, tide and dream, and a strong want can be gone by morning.

With a partner it's absorbing their mood until you can't find your own wants in the fog. In the body it's a tiredness that comes from feeling too much with no wall up. With sleep it's vivid dreams carrying the wanting your waking self lets slip. When a real want surfaces, write it down before it goes, and treat the note as a promise you've made yourself.
moon.reversed:
Inverted, the card can have a Pisces Moon drowning its own wants in everyone else's feelings. Mars through Neptune dissolves what wall you had, so the pull toward your own bigger life gets lost under the moods you soak up from the room, and you can't tell any more which wants are yours. It can tip into escape, numbing, a drift toward whatever softens the edges, and the wanting goes quiet under the fog.

With a partner it shows as losing yourself so completely in their needs that yours vanish. In the body it's a heavy, foggy tiredness from taking in too much. With sleep it's too much of it, or dreams that leave you wearier than when you went to bed. Name one want that's actually yours, write it where you'll see it, and keep one hour in the week for it that belongs to nobody else.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly, taking on the colour of whoever's in front of you, and people find you gentle, receptive, a little hard to pin down. This card asks for a clear, pointed beginning, which is a stretch for an Ascendant that would sooner flow around an obstacle. Aries is your next-door neighbour in the zodiac, and neighbours have little in common, so the card's decisiveness and your adaptability sit side by side without quite understanding each other. Mars arrives through Jupiter or Neptune, so what you're after comes across as a mood, a feel, and people have to guess at the plan.

Fire and water clash here, so the bold start the card wants can feel like it might scald you, and you tend to melt the pressure away. Mars in your Ten of Cups decan means you start best when the aim is warmth, people and belonging. The Moon, your Major, makes your surface reflective, so strangers often meet a version of themselves in you before they meet you.

At a first meeting it's being wonderfully easy to talk to and leaving them unsure what you want. In dating it's merging so fast you lose your own edges. At a new job you become everybody's confidant and nobody's obvious choice for the bigger role. When you next start something with a new person, name one specific thing you want from it, out loud, early on.
rising.reversed:
Softness is Pisces rising's gift, and with this card reversed it turns into something people can't get hold of. The receptiveness that usually feels gentle reads as vague or evasive, and Mars through Neptune blurs your first moves so much that strangers aren't sure what you want, or even quite who you are. Or you take on so much of their colour that they feel they're talking to a mirror, and it unsettles them.

In a new role it's being pleasant and somehow overlooked, hard to place. On a first date it's agreeing with everything and leaving them nothing solid to hold. In a new circle it's dissolving into the mood and disappearing. Say one clear, slightly firm thing about what you think or want early on, and let people meet that edge of you.

1.upright:
The first house is your body, your bearing and the way you start things, and this card could hardly be more at home in it. Mars is the natural ruler of the first house and Aries is its natural sign, and the Two of Wands is Mars in Aries, so the card is standing on its own ground twice over. Fire meets fire, and everything gets louder. It's an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever gets stirred up here shows quickly, in how you walk into a room and how fast you say yes to things.

With the card this much at home, the urge to expand runs strong and easy, and the danger is the ordinary danger of too much of a good thing. You can feel ready to claim new ground before you've decided which ground. That readiness passes for a plan, and mostly it's appetite.
